claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 8 years old and I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I can see you have one child, Alex, who is 8 years old.

Let me ask you some questions to determine your eligibility:

**Do you live in the UK, and does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK and Alex lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. That's helpful information.

**Are you responsible for Alex's care - meaning you provide for his needs such as food, clothes, and general upkeep?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I am responsible for Alex. I provide for all his needs - food, clothes, everything he needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for confirming that.

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

Just a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is Alex in any of these situations:**
- In hospital or residential accommodation for an extended period?
- Living in care (provided by the local council)?
- Working 24 hours or more per week?
- Receiving benefits in his own right (such as Universal Credit)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, actually Alex has been in hospital for a while now - it's been a few months. But other than that, no - he's not in care, he doesn't work, and he doesn't receive any benefits himself.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for sharing that. I need to understand a bit more about Alex's hospital stay to assess your eligibility properly.

**How many weeks has Alex been in hospital?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's been there for 15 weeks now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since Alex has been in hospital for 15 weeks (which is more than 12 weeks), this affects your Child Benefit entitlement. However, there's an important exception:

**Do you regularly spend money on Alex while he's in hospital?** (For example, on things like clothes, toys, treats, or other items for him)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not sure... I mean, I want to, but with everything going on, I honestly don't know if what I've been doing counts as "regularly" or not. It's been difficult.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I completely understand - this is a difficult situation and it's understandable that you're unsure.

Let me ask this to help clarify: **Have you been buying things for Alex or spending money on him at all during his hospital stay?** For example, even occasionally buying him items, gifts, or anything else?

It would help me understand whether you might qualify for the exception to the 12-week rule.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I really don't know how to answer that properly. Some weeks I've managed to get things for him, other times I haven't been able to. I'm just not certain if it's been regular enough or what counts.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand, and thank you for being honest about your situation. It sounds like you have been making some efforts to spend money on Alex, but you're genuinely uncertain whether it meets the requirement of being "regular" enough.

Let me ask one final question to make sure I have all the information:

**Are you and Alex both living in the UK normally, or are there any circumstances involving living abroad or immigration status (such as pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme) that I should know about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, we both live in the UK normally. There's nothing about living abroad or any immigration issues - we're just regular UK residents.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me summarize your situation and provide my assessment:

- Alex is 8 years old and lives with you in the UK (when not in hospital)
- You are responsible for his care and provide for his needs
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him
- However, Alex has been in hospital for 15 weeks (exceeding the 12-week threshold)
- You have made some financial contributions toward Alex during his hospital stay, but you're uncertain whether these have been regular enough to qualify for the exception

Based on the rules, when a child has been in hospital for more than 12 weeks, you can continue to receive Child Benefit if you "regularly spend money on them." However, given that you genuinely do not have sufficient information to confirm whether your spending has been regular enough to meet this requirement, I cannot definitively determine whether you would qualify for this exception.

**Assessment Complete: INDETERMINATE**

Based on the information you've provided, I cannot make a definitive determination about your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

**Here's why:**

You meet all the basic eligibility requirements:
- Alex is 8 years old (under 16)
- You live in the UK
- Alex normally lives with you
- You're responsible for his care
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him

**However,** since Alex has been in hospital for 15 weeks (more than the 12-week limit), your Child Benefit would normally stop unless you meet an exception. The key exception is that you can continue receiving Child Benefit if you **regularly spend money on Alex** while he's in hospital.

You've indicated that you have spent some money on him, but you're genuinely uncertain whether this has been regular enough to meet the requirement.

**My recommendation:** I would strongly encourage you to **contact HMRC's Child Benefit Office directly** to discuss your specific situation. They can:
- Review the details of your spending on Alex
- Help you understand whether what you've been doing counts as "regular" spending
- Make a formal determination about your eligibility

They are best placed to assess your individual circumstances and provide a definitive answer.
